In Sullivan Station, Surrey, the 55+ homes you can buy are Charleston Green and Sullivan Mews (strata and co-op or membership). This page names each building, says what type it is and what the sources show, and covers local rules and the questions buyers ask. Anything no source states is marked unconfirmed.
55+ strata buildings you can buy in Sullivan Station
Gated 55+ townhouse complex, freehold strata, plan NWS2625, built 1988; listings describe it as a "gated 55+ townhouse complex" with a clubhouse and pets allowed. Unit count: UNCONFIRMED.
55+ co-op and membership housing in Sullivan Station (not strata)

The name trap, stated plainly: MLS listings place this complex in the East Newton sub-area, not Sullivan Station, despite the name. It is a retirement community with a 55+ age restriction, a maximum of 2 occupants, no smoking and 1 small pet — and it is NOT a strata: the listing states "This is not Strata. It is a membership therefore not mortgages possible" and that a purchase must be cash, with a monthly fee ($540 in the listing) covering taxes, heat, electricity, management, insurance and water.
Streets, schools and getting around Sullivan Station

items.t: Municipality and community: City of Surrey, in the Newton community. The City's South Newton plan page describes South Newton as a large neighbourhood within the southeast of the broader Newton community, with neighbourhood commercial nodes including Panorama Heights at 152 Street and Hwy 10 and Sullivan Heights at 64 Ave and 144 Street — the Sullivan Station board sub-area sits inside that South Newton ground.

"Sullivan Station" is the SnapStats / board sub-area name for Surrey in the September 2026 report; the City does not publish a separate "Sullivan Station" plan boundary — the City names in this ground are "Sullivan," "Sullivan Heights" and "South Newton." A City boundary line for Sullivan Station itself: UNVERIFIED.

Plan area: the South Newton plan area is approximately 485 hectares (1,200 acres), generally located north of Hwy 10, east of King George Boulevard and west of 152 Street, bordered by the East Newton NCPs to the northwest.

Current plan status: the South Newton plan was rescinded by the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan update and is no longer in effect; development in this area is led by the Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 21900), and on December 2, 2024 Council endorsed Corporate Report R246, which updated land use designations to reflect current market conditions.
Nearby areas: Panorama Ridge (south, across the Highway 10 side of South Newton), East Newton (northwest), West Newton (west), Cloverdale (east, across the 152 Street side).

Where Newton's verified 55+ housing actually is, relative to this sub-area: East Newton (Chelsea Gardens, Charleston Green, Sullivan Mews membership complex, Arbourside Court retirement residence) and Panorama Ridge (Lakewood Heights, Lakewood Place) — surrounding this sub-area on two sides, with none inside it.

blocks.text: Local rules and plans in Sullivan Station

items.t: City zoning: Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 12000: governs the sub-area; MLS data for the neighbouring Chelsea Gardens records its zoning as RM45.

Plans: the South Newton plan no longer exists as a governing document: It was rescinded by the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan update (OCP Bylaw No. 21900, adopted June 15, 2026, replacing Bylaw 18020), and development in this area is led by the OCP; on December 2, 2024 Council endorsed Corporate Report R246, which updated South Newton's land use designations to reflect current market conditions. Read the current OCP and Zoning Bylaw 12000, not the rescinded plan.

Small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH): Surrey allows a maximum of 3 units on lots smaller than 280 m², 4 units on lots larger than 280 m², and up to 6 units on eligible lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent bus stop — the route for a Sullivan Station 55+ homeowner to add a suite or units on a detached lot.

Manufactured-home parks in Surrey carry a City policy layer on top of the provincial Act: the City's Manufactured Home Park Policy brochure tells park residents the property owner must give 12 months' notice of a final moving date, can only give that notice after receiving all permits and approvals, and must pay $20,000 on or before the move-out date. Surrey's Tenant Protection Bylaw, 2025, No. 21788 does NOT apply to property governed by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act. (No park is verified inside this sub-area; the policy is the city-wide frame.)

Property taxes (city-wide): City of Surrey property taxes are due July 2, with a 5% penalty if not paid by midnight July 2 and a further 5% penalty after September 2. The Province's regular property tax deferment program is for people 55 and older.

Good to know about Sullivan Station

items.t: The sub-area's governing plan was rescinded, not amended. The South Newton plan is no longer in effect at all — the Surrey 2050 OCP update removed it, and Corporate Report R246 (December 2, 2024) redrew the designations. Any page still walking a buyer through "the South Newton plan" is describing a dead document.

The "Sullivan" 55+ complex is not in Sullivan Station. Sullivan Mews sits at 15020 66A Ave and MLS files it under East Newton; the name, the sub-area and the tenure (membership, not strata) all mislead in different directions, and all three are corrected in.

Sullivan Station is ringed by 55+ stock it does not contain. East Newton's Chelsea Gardens / Charleston Green to the northwest and Panorama Ridge's Lakewood pair to the south are the sub-area's real 55+ market — a buyer searching "Sullivan Station 55+" will be shown all of them by the portals, under three different sub-area labels.

faq.q: Is there any 55+ housing in Sullivan Station itself?
faq.a: No — none was verified in any source. The sub-area's named complexes (The Uplands, Seneca Woods, Ashbury Hill, Altura, Panorama West Coast Living, Cambridge Park, Creekside Terrace) are family product with no age restriction in any source checked.

faq.q: What about Sullivan Mews? It has "Sullivan" in the name.
faq.a: Sullivan Mews (15020 66A Ave) is a genuine 55+ complex — but MLS places it in the East Newton sub-area, and it is not a strata: it is a membership purchase ("not mortgages possible," cash purchase, monthly fee covering taxes, heat, electricity, management, insurance and water, per the listing).

faq.q: Where is the nearest actual 55+ purchase to Sullivan Station?
faq.a: North, in East Newton: Chelsea Gardens (13870 / 13888 70 Ave, gated, plan LMS1416) and Charleston Green (6537 138 St, gated townhouses, built 1988). South, in Panorama Ridge: Lakewood Heights (6211 W Boundary Dr) and Lakewood Place (6061 W Boundary Dr).

faq.q: Can I add a suite or extra units to a Sullivan Station detached house for a caregiver or family member?
faq.a: Surrey's SSMUH rules allow 3 units on lots smaller than 280 m², 4 units on lots larger than 280 m², and up to 6 units on eligible lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent bus stop.

faq.q: Is the old South Newton plan still the rulebook for this area?
faq.a: No. The South Newton plan was rescinded by the Surrey 2050 OCP update and is no longer in effect; the OCP (Bylaw No. 21900) leads, with designations updated by Corporate Report R246 (endorsed December 2, 2024).

faq.q: Can I defer my property taxes at 55+?
faq.a: The Province's Benefits Connector states the regular property tax deferment loan program is for people 55 and older (plus surviving spouses and persons with disabilities), and the additional home owner grant (total $845 in Metro Vancouver / Fraser Valley) is for seniors 65+.
